آشِرٌ Dividing [or sawing], or one who divides [or saws], wood, with the مِئْشَار (Msb.) ―
-b2- [Hence,] The prickles [or serrated parts] of the shanks of the locust; (K;) as also ↓ تَآشِيرُ (TA.) ―
-b3- Also, and ↓ أُشْرَةٌ and ↓ عُقْدَةٌ ) at the extremity of the tail of the locust, like two claws; (K;) which two things are also called ↓ أُشْرَتَانِ and ↓ مِئْشَارَانِ (TA.) ―
-b4- آشِرَةٌ A woman who sharpens the extremities of her teeth [and makes them serrated: see 1]. (Msb.) ＝
-A2- يَدٌ آشِرَةٌ An arm, or a hand, sawn off; i. q. ↓ مَأْشُورَةٌ : (ISk, S, Msb, K:*) like عِيشَةٌ رَاضِيَةٌ in the sense of مَرْضِيَةٌ. (S.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
